source.snippet: Since February 2026, I am seeing huge spikes in (Spain located) Internet accessible servers (nginx, apache, tomcat) due to AI bots crawling for content. Is there a recommended way to address this? I am using the typical reactive way of automatically throttling IPs with custom scripts, but wanted to know if there is a better way. The least proxies, software, containers I can put the better, servers already struggling due to internal AIs deployments.

problem_statement: Server operators managing public-facing web infrastructure face severe performance degradation from aggressive AI crawler bots since early 2026, and existing reactive IP-throttling scripts are insufficient — they need a lightweight, low-overhead solution that doesn't add more proxy or container layers to already-strained servers.
target_segment: SMB and mid-market DevOps/sysadmin teams running nginx/apache/tomcat on self-managed servers with limited resources
notes: Buyer context: business-critical servers already paying for hosting infra; operator is spending engineering time on custom scripts — a clear 'time costs money' signal. Pain onset is recent and acute (Feb 2026). Multiple server types mentioned (nginx, apache, tomcat), suggesting a cross-stack need. Willingness to pay implied by desire for a managed/better solution over DIY scripts. Competing products (Cloudflare, Nginx rate-limit modules) exist but require adding proxies the buyer explicitly wants to avoid.
